## 固定收益開篇論點

美國與伊朗停火破裂，推動油價大幅上漲；聯準會6月會議紀要則顯示，緊縮政策已成為決策委員會正在考慮、但內部分歧的情境。受此影響，美國公債在7月8日延續賣壓，2年期殖利率上升3.3個基點至4.22%，5年期上升3.9個基點至4.328%，10年期上升2.9個基點至4.581%，30年期上升1.7個基點至5.074%。各天期普遍承壓，但賣壓集中於短、中天期，反映市場將聯準會下一次可能升息的時點提前，而非僅將地緣政治升溫視為長期通膨或財政衝擊。

美國發動新一輪空襲並撤銷允許伊朗出售石油的豁免後，總統川普宣布臨時停火實際上已告終。布蘭特原油上漲5.21%至每桶$78.02，WTI上漲4.37%至$73.52。豁免遭撤銷，也使約6,300萬桶伊朗原油滯留海上或等待買家；針對荷莫茲海峽航運的新一輪威脅，則提高了現貨供給趨緊的風險，即使全球總產量仍然充裕亦然。

美國原油庫存表面增加，卻不足以消除成品油供應偏緊的問題。截至7月3日當週，商業原油庫存增加300萬桶，但汽油庫存減少190萬桶，餾分油庫存減少500萬桶，煉油廠產能利用率已達95.8%。餾分油庫存約低於5年同期平均12%。因此，單看原油庫存增加會低估新一輪油價衝擊傳導至終端燃料成本的風險。

聯準會會議紀要進一步支持殖利率走升。雖然決策委員會在6月16日至17日的會議上一致將聯邦基金利率維持於3.5%至3.75%，少數官員已認為當時有升息理由。決策官員普遍判斷通膨上行風險仍高，就業下行風險則略有緩和。最廣義而言，利率預測正好各占一半：9位官員預期2026年至少升息1碼，其中6位預期至少升息2碼；另外9位預期利率不變或調降。主席Kevin Warsh未提交預測。

市場反應並非不加區分地押注通膨。10年期實質殖利率上升2.4個基點至2.305%，10年期損益兩平通膨率僅上升0.5個基點至2.276%，顯示名目指標殖利率的漲幅大多來自實質利率。這與市場更加相信聯準會將因應持續性通膨，而不會容忍通膨預期持續上升的看法一致。2年與10年期利差縮小0.4個基點至36.1個基點，2年與30年期利差則縮小1.6個基點至85.4個基點。

儘管如此，財政部增額發行的$390億10年期公債需求仍穩健。得標殖利率為4.580%，較標售前市場殖利率低約0.6個基點，投標倍數為2.59倍。間接投標人獲配$317.21億的競爭性投標，主要交易商承接$30.27億。即使油價、偏鷹政策情境及異常龐大的公司債供給持續對整體折現率環境構成壓力，較高的殖利率仍吸引投資人增加利率部位。

風險資產並未引發資金全面轉進政府公債。標普500指數收復大部分早盤跌幅，收盤下跌0.28%；那斯達克100指數上漲0.27%，費城半導體指數上漲2.23%。儘管地緣政治情勢升溫，黃金仍下跌1.79%，美元指數也下滑0.09%。上市投資級、高收益及新興市場債券基金約下跌0.13%至0.19%，信用違約交換利差則自異常緊窄的水準擴大。整體而言，本交易日同時出現通膨風險重燃及實質殖利率上升，但風險趨避仍具選擇性，並非系統性撤退。

## 油價與聯準會將政策時程推前

這波立即重定價，始於荷莫茲海峽周邊政治及實際航運情勢惡化。川普表示，與伊朗談判已是浪費時間，並威脅追加空襲、再次封鎖伊朗港口。美國此前已攻擊逾80處地點，並撤銷允許伊朗出售石油的臨時豁免。德黑蘭指控美國違反臨時協議，警告將採取報復行動，並堅稱船隻未經伊朗許可不得通過海峽。

布蘭特原油在美國交易時段升破$79，隨後交易一度超過$80，收回6月休戰後的部分跌幅；不過，以一個月計算，布蘭特仍下跌16.19%，WTI也下跌18.80%。對貨幣政策而言，關鍵並非油價重返戰時高峰，而是快速反轉的通膨降溫趨勢再次受到干擾；先前正是這波降溫，促使投資人把下一次預期升息推遲至今年較晚時點。

撤銷石油銷售豁免，使供給問題不再局限於油輪航行的直接風險。約6,300萬桶伊朗原油已裝載於波斯灣及亞洲海域的船隻上，其中許多船舶未顯示明確目的地，或仍在尋找買家。臨時協議達成後，至少有19批伊朗石油及石化貨物完成裝船，伊朗沿岸另有46艘滿載油輪被辨識出來。

潛在買家原本就相當謹慎：歐洲與英國的限制仍然有效，保險不易取得，港口也可能拒絕與伊朗影子船隊有關的船舶。日本、台灣及南韓煉油商雖收到報價，卻未有買進紀錄；印度業者則僅在美國豁免延長至8月以後的前提下才準備採購。中國獨立煉油商仍可能接手，但沙烏地阿拉伯與伊拉克供給形成競爭，意味德黑蘭可能必須提供大幅折價。因此，豁免撤銷不但取消了和平安排中承諾給予伊朗的收入，也讓大量原油在商業上難以找到出路。

美國石油數據說明，市場為何同時關注成品油與原油供給。不含戰略石油儲備的商業原油庫存增至4.114億桶，但仍比5年同期平均低約6%。汽油庫存在當週下降後，也比平均水準低約6%。餾分油庫存降至1.036億桶，較同期常態低約12%；商業石油總庫存則減少400萬桶。煉油廠平均每日加工1,700萬桶原油，產能利用率達95.8%，短期內已很難單靠提高開工率彌補成品油庫存進一步減少。

這組供需條件強化了通膨傳導。如果面臨威脅的原油仍能抵達買家，原油的地緣政治溢價可能迅速消退；但汽油與餾分油庫存偏低，會提高供應中斷傳導至零售及運輸成本的機率。美國平均汽油價格5月已升至每加侖$4.56以上，之後回落近17%，至7月6日為$3.79。最新一波油價反彈可能侵蝕部分改善，但尚未形成另一波持續上漲。

聯準會6月會議紀要提供了市場評價能源風險時所依據的政策反應。官員表示通膨仍高，並普遍認為物價穩定面臨的風險偏向上行。另一方面，多項勞動指標顯示就業保持穩定，對充分就業明顯轉弱的擔憂已有所降低。決策委員會仍預期2026年剩餘時間的實質GDP將穩健成長。

決策官員討論的是截然不同的政策路徑，並未就無條件升息形成共識。若通膨降溫，多數官員預期維持、或最終調降目標利率區間；若人工智慧相關需求強勁、能源價格偏高及關稅導致通膨持續，多數官員則認為可能需要進一步緊縮。紀要確認，面對持續性壓力，再次升息仍是可採取的因應措施，因此支持殖利率上升；但若通膨消退，維持利率或最終降息的可能性依然存在。

個別預測的分布更凸顯內部缺乏共識。9位與會者預期今年至少升息一次，其中6位預期至少升息兩次；其餘9位預期不升息或降息，Warsh則未提出預測。少數官員認為6月已具備升息理由，但仍加入一致維持利率不變的表決。兩者的差異十分重要：會議紀要顯示政策風險分布轉趨鷹派，並不代表下次會議已決定升息。

市場因此把下一次預期升息時點從12月提前至10月。一項盤中指標顯示，7月會議升息機率接近33%；另一項指標顯示機率超過30%，高於前一個星期四的不到20%。更廣泛的市場定價則反映年底前升息逾1碼。這些機率形成時，衝突與能源價格後續路徑仍不得而知，使地緣政治結果對政策時程的影響格外重要。

實質殖利率走勢符合這項解讀。10年期TIPS殖利率升至2.305%，來到2025年4月以來的最高區域，並較一個月前高14.3個基點。10年期通膨補償率7月8日僅小幅上升，仍較一個月前低9.3個基點。投資人因市場反映央行將採取更強硬的對策，而要求更高的通膨調整後報酬；原油自先前戰時高點回落，則持續壓抑較長期的通膨補償。

這波轉變發生於交易活躍的市場。FINRA記錄的美國公債面額交易量為$1.441兆，較前一交易日增加20.7%；其中名目附息債交易量增加24.4%至$1.1402兆。逾7年、但不超過10年期債券的交易量增加41.8%至$2,259億，TIPS交易量則增加55.6%至$235億。這些數據衡量雙向成交，不能直接代表買賣方向，但顯示殖利率重定價及標售前讓利發生於交投熱絡的市場。

## 批發銷售穩健、信用卡信貸轉弱，標售需求強勁

美國經濟活動數據並未為通膨風險提供明確抵銷。5月批發銷售較4月成長3.4%至$8,174億，較上年同期增加18.1%；4月月增率則由2%上修至2.2%。庫存僅增加0.1%至$9,418億，較上年同期高4%；存貨銷售比由2025年5月的1.31降至1.15。

這組數據顯示名目交易額強勁，但相對銷售而言，商品庫存更加精簡。批發活動對本季經濟成長形成較強支撐；然而，存貨比率偏低，也表示若供應中斷或運輸成本上升妨礙補庫，企業可運用的緩衝較少。報告無法判斷銷售成長有多少來自數量、有多少來自價格，但並不支持需求全面崩落的看法。

消費者信貸則傳遞不同的家庭部門訊號。5月信貸總額以經季節調整年率計算持平，4月增幅則修正為4.9%。年化資金流由修正後的增加$2,499億轉為減少$22億，經季節調整的信貸餘額為$5.1545兆。

信貸組成比總額更弱。包含信用卡餘額的循環信貸以4.7%的年率萎縮，非循環信貸則成長1.6%。即使批發銷售仍強，信用卡借款轉為收縮，顯示家庭支出從短期信貸取得的支撐減少。這也呈現不同於油價的另一條傳導管道：消費者不再擴張循環信貸之際，燃料成本上升可能進一步壓縮其可自由支配現金流。

美國公債供給端並未出現類似的需求流失。增額發行的$390億10年期公債以4.580%得標，創該天期自2025年2月以來最高標售殖利率，並較標售前交易水準低約0.6個基點。投標倍數為2.59倍；間接投標人獲配$317.21億，直接投標人獲配$41.75億，主要交易商承接$30.27億。該債券於7月15日交割，2036年5月15日到期。

標售結果未能扭轉當日賣壓，但證明10年期殖利率接近4.6%時，買方願意承接指標債券的利率風險。間接投標帳戶取得大部分獲接受的競爭性投標，交易商獲配有限，降低了中介機構必須立即承擔的庫存。這項需求尤其值得注意，因為標售前一週殖利率已大幅上升，且當時全球債市正在遭遇賣壓，而非受惠於資金避險。

17週期國庫券標售也吸引大量現金需求。財政部發行$720億、期限119天的國庫券，最高利率為3.790%，投資收益率為3.891%。投標倍數達3.41倍，收到$2,436.46億競爭性投標，接受其中$703.71億。間接投標人獲配$489.86億，直接投標人獲配$31.58億，主要交易商承接$182.27億。該券於7月14日交割，11月10日到期。

國庫券標售結果顯示，約4個月期資金市場沒有明顯壓力；不過，其所處曲線區段不同於對聯準會政策敏感的2年期公債。即使市場提高再次升息的機率，現金投資人的投標金額仍超過發行量3倍。在3.790%最高利率獲配的比例高達80.43%，代表標售結果集中於該得標利率，並非相對標售前參考水準表現疲弱。

下一次供給考驗將移至殖利率曲線更長端。財政部將於7月9日增額發行$220億、票息5%的公債，距到期尚有29年10個月，並與10年期增額發行債券同於7月15日交割。30年期殖利率已高於5%，此次標售將檢驗指標10年期債券所見的需求，能否延伸至承擔更高財政不確定性及期限溢價風險的長天期債券。

## 緊縮訊號擴散至已開發與新興市場

美債走勢是全球債券賣壓的一部分。隨投資人提高對歐洲央行及英格蘭銀行進一步緊縮的押注，歐洲殖利率漲勢更加明顯。英國10年期公債殖利率跳升10個基點至4.95%，創近一個月最高。儘管油價與聯準會會議紀要仍是美國市場最強的國內催化因素，全球同步重定價顯示，美債賣壓並非只是在反映美國數據。

紐西蘭已實際採取緊縮行動。紐西蘭央行將官方現金利率提高25個基點至2.5%，為3年來首次升息；由於通膨仍高於目標，且經濟活動預計增強，央行表示可能需要進一步減少貨幣刺激。決策公布後，紐西蘭元及政府公債殖利率上升。此舉強化全球朝政策收緊方向重定價的趨勢，但反映的是紐西蘭央行對本國情勢的評估，不代表各國央行遵循共同時程。

波蘭連續第4個月將政策利率維持於3.75%，符合全部29位經濟學家的預測，但上調通膨預估。央行目前預期2026年消費者物價成長2.4%至3.3%，高於3月預測的1.6%至2.9%；經濟成長預測區間則由3.1%至4.7%調整為3%至4.4%。6月通膨雖已放緩至2.5%，但中東不確定性及能源成本，使近期恢復降息的可能性降低。

遠期利率協議上升4個基點，顯示波蘭政策利率可能在2026年剩餘時間維持不變。通膨預測上修後，整體通膨回到央行目標區間的意義下降：決策官員固然已沒有明確理由進一步緊縮，但預測路徑也未改善到足以恢復降息。央行總裁Adam Glapinski於7月9日舉行的簡報，將顯示官員更重視當前通膨改善，還是外部價格風險再起。

羅馬尼亞也維持利率不變，指標利率保持在6.5%，為歐盟最高，符合市場一致預期。先前能源衝擊加上稅負及電價上限取消的影響，使5月通膨重新升破10%。央行預期通膨6月將小幅下降，第三季則會隨基期效應消退而大幅回落；較長期而言，財政整頓也將抑制需求。

不過，這項預期中的通膨降溫易受政治及財政執行影響。總理Ilie Bolojan未通過信任投票後，羅馬尼亞目前由看守政府執政，各政黨仍未就繼任內閣達成共識。立法僵局若持續，可能阻礙取得歐盟復甦基金所需的措施，並提高主權評等遭調降的風險。羅馬尼亞的評等已位於投資級最低一級，而且3大評等機構的展望均為負向。

智利則出現較立即的通膨意外。6月消費者物價較5月持平，市場原先預期下降0.2%；年通膨率加速至4.3%，創去年9月以來最高，並高於3%的目標。能源價格下跌1.1%，運輸價格在燃料走低的幫助下下降1.3%，服飾價格則因Cyber Day促銷而下跌6.1%；食品及非酒精飲料上漲0.8%，抵銷了上述降幅。

數據顯示，經濟活動疲弱尚未帶來全面通膨降溫。智利經濟活動指數在4月幾乎沒有成長後於5月下滑，失業率已達9.4%，分析師預期2026年GDP僅成長1.6%。然而，CPI公布後，2年期交換利率上升10個基點至4.46%；食品價格壓力加上全球能源風險再起，也支持央行審慎地把政策利率維持在4.5%。

日本債市則面臨強勁信貸活動、政治力量對貨幣政策的影響，以及財政融資問題未解之間格外直接的衝突。6月銀行放款較上年同期成長6.3%，創2020年8月以來最快增速，動能來自併購、房地產及經濟復甦。日本央行6月已將指標利率升至1%，但數據顯示信貸取得仍然順暢。

放款數據強化了日本經濟有能力承受進一步政策正常化的看法。企業對金融情勢的評估一年來首次改善，大型企業也表示商業本票發行條件轉佳。日本實質政策利率仍低於零；日本央行估計，在排除暫時性因素及生鮮食品後，基礎通膨高於2%。不過，民間對最終利率水準的預測仍有差異：6月會議後受訪的經濟學家預期終端利率為1.75%，法國巴黎銀行則預估為2.5%，約每4至5個月升息一次。

政府措辭的改變未能緩解長天期日本公債的壓力。年度經濟財政方針的最新草案，新增貨幣政策應有助於物價穩定上漲的要求；這項措辭可被解讀為允許日本央行在必要時升息。先前草案僅強調適當執行貨幣政策的重要性，未提及通膨，因而引發市場擔憂高市早苗政府希望抑制進一步升息。

文字修改仍未阻止賣壓。10年及20年期日本公債殖利率升至1996年以來最高，投資人持續關注高市政府計畫在2040財政年度前，對17個策略產業投入¥370兆公私部門資金的目標，以及政府本身將負擔多少融資仍不明朗。由高市委任、也是唯一反對6月升息的日本央行審議委員Toichiro Asada另行警告，利率上升可能拖慢經濟。另一位被視為支持通貨再膨脹政策的任命人選Ayano Sato，將於7月底首次出席會議。

穆迪表示，日本A1評等及穩定展望目前仍維持平衡。該機構援引穩定成長、持續通膨，以及政府債務占GDP比率預計由2020財政年度約219%，降至2030年的195%以下。不過，穆迪也把經常性支出、財政整頓轉弱，以及投資計畫中民間參與不足列為潛在風險。這項評估未能消除市場疑慮：若財政擴張與限制日本央行正常化同時發生，可能使通膨與日圓疲弱更加根深蒂固。

中國主權債市場面臨相反的需求問題。10年期政府公債標售的投標倍數達到7.23倍，創2004年開始統計以來最高。平均殖利率為1.7249%，最高殖利率為1.7418%，可比債券在次級市場的交易殖利率約為1.728%。貸款需求疲弱，促使銀行持續尋求公債配置；一級市場手續費回饋取消後，標售定價也更透明，並在標售殖利率高於次級市場時創造套利機會。

## 信用投資人承接供給，但提高篩選要求

停火破裂使信用市場小幅走弱，但價格走勢遠未達到全面融資凍結的程度。投資級債券基金LQD下跌0.19%，高收益債券基金HYG下跌0.13%，JNK下跌0.16%，新興市場債券基金EMB下跌0.16%。美國與歐洲的信用違約交換利差，均自接近全球金融危機後低點的水準擴大。即使現券損失有限，這項走勢仍顯示地緣政治風險足以擾動估值處於歷史高檔的市場。

面對幾乎沒有犯錯空間的估值，投資人行為已開始調整。美國非傳統債券基金資產今年增加約6%，較2024年底增加18%；歐洲全球彈性債券基金資產則在2026年擴張近10%。這些策略不必依照指數權重買進證券，可以在政府公債、公司債、次順位工具及衍生性商品之間調整。此類策略重新受到青睞，既反映整體殖利率具有吸引力，也顯示投資人對普遍緊窄的信用利差愈加不安。

科技業大量發債，正加深發行人品質與市場承接能力之間的差異。Amazon的$250億發債交易吸引$410億訂單，相當於發行規模的1.6倍，遠低於2月前一次Amazon發債的4.7倍。該公司今年發債金額已超過$900億，並使超大規模雲端業者的新債供給達約$1,940億。

美國銀行分析師估計，Amazon發債使既有超大規模雲端業者債券的利差在前一交易日擴大6至15個基點，並為當日10年期美債殖利率漲幅貢獻約8個基點。這項估算顯示，大型人工智慧融資不只是產業信用事件，也是利率市場議題：交易商與投資人必須以足以影響公司債定價基準——美國公債——的規模，為相關利率風險籌資及避險。

這並不代表買方已退出。Amazon完成了融資，半導體股也在7月8日反彈，公司債整體殖利率仍遠高於長期平均。不過，接連出現的巨額交易，確實要求市場提供更多資產負債表承作能力，也讓價格敏感度提高。被動式信用投資人尤其容易受到影響，因為發行人的借款愈多，在指數中的權重便愈高，可能使投資組合更加集中於創造最多新供給的公司。

較弱發行人的壓力則明顯得多。Aston Martin於2029年到期的$10.5億有擔保票據下跌約4美分，至每1美元面額約72美分；超過半數有擔保票據持有人已組成合作團體。該團體由Akin Gump擔任顧問，仍開放其他有擔保債權人加入。豪華車製造商因獲利壓力而被迫裁員、重新評估新車款並尋找非傳統現金來源之際，合作團體讓債券持有人得以透過共同架構參與談判。

Victoria已與先前交易中遭排除的2028年到期票據持有人達成重整協議。同意方案的持有人將以原證券面額75%的價值，取得2031年到期的新第二順位債券，以及公司約19%的股權。持有£1.666億未償票據三分之二的一個團體支持該計畫。投資人在10個營業日內加入，可取得提前同意費；不同意者則面臨債券價值被減記至零。

這家地毯製造商也與Koch議定條件；後者將以£3.8億優先工具，換取£0.5億優先股、25%的普通股權，以及2031年到期的新第二順位債券。Victoria預期合併重整將使債務與優先順位負債減少逾£3億。交易化解了去年上調部分債權優先順位所引發的部分債權人爭議，但代價是大幅讓步與股權稀釋，而非恢復一般融資。

主權借款人的融資選擇更加多元。阿根廷已籌得7月9日到期的$43億半年度外幣債券付款所需資金，並確認了計畫中的融資來源，以在不依賴國際市場發債的情況下，支付至總統Javier Milei於2027年任期結束前的債務。約$40億財政部美元存款，加上即將到位、由多邊機構支持的融資，將支應本次付款。

阿根廷自3月以來，透過在國內發行2027年及2028年到期的美元債券，已籌得約$40億，平均殖利率為6.9%，低於投資人估計其在國際市場發債須支付的約8.6%。較低的國內成本，解釋了政府為何不願只為證明能重返全球市場而發債。風險在於，2027年融資計畫幾乎沒有容錯空間：明年約有$250億債務到期，預定由國內發債、央行買進美元、IMF撥款、民營化收入，以及2026年結轉現金支應。

孟加拉的資本市場發展仍處於較早階段。政府將成立跨部會小組，研究首次海外主權債券的架構、時點及可行性。官員尚未決定規模或幣別；一般美元債是主要選項，也曾討論發行熊貓債。政府計畫增加19%支出，這項發債方案可使融資來源不再只依賴國內銀行及優惠性多邊貸款，但也會讓財政計畫直接接受國際定價與信用評等檢視。

約翰尼斯堡則計畫在7月中以前，向包括Rand Water及Eskom在內的債權人支付近24億南非蘭特欠款，以恢復遭扣留的政府移轉款。南非財政部已扣留對69個地方政府支付的135億蘭特；待地方政府提交可接受的還款計畫後，初期僅會撥付其中約三分之一。剩餘資金是否釋出，部分取決於地方政府能否在9月底前將未經授權、不合規及浪費性支出至少削減25%。市長Dada Morero表示，市政府也在籌備發債，以支應基礎設施修繕，但交易顧問與最終條件尚未確定。

## 前瞻市場意義

7月9日美國市場的第一項考驗，是美東時間08:30公布的初領失業救濟金人數。數據將顯示，勞動市場是否仍處於招聘放緩、勞動流動性下降，但裁員未全面增加的狀態。這項區別正是理解聯準會會議紀要的關鍵：官員對就業下行風險的擔憂略有降低，因而在政策反應中賦予持續性通膨更高權重。

6月成屋銷售將於美東時間10:00公布。隨美債殖利率再次走升，銷售與庫存數據將提供住宅市場對房貸利率敏感度的最新衡量，也有助判斷5月循環信貸收縮，究竟是信用卡借款的局部現象，還是更廣泛的家庭需求放緩。

當日最直接的長天期事件，是財政部於美東時間13:00增額發行$220億、票息5%的30年期公債。該券距到期尚有29年10個月，並於7月15日交割。10年期增額發行吸引強勁的間接投標需求，得標殖利率也低於標售前市場水準；但30年期公債承擔更高的財政不確定性、期限溢價及通膨持續性風險。得標殖利率相對標售前交易的表現，以及間接、直接投標人與交易商的獲配分布，將決定週三所見需求能否延伸至曲線最長端。

日本央行7月地區經濟報告將更新各地工資、物價及經濟活動資訊；此前銀行放款已成長6.3%，長天期日本公債殖利率也升至數十年高點。即使政治層面擔憂借款成本上升，報告仍將直接影響市場對寬鬆金融條件是否足以支持進一步政策正常化的判斷。政府年度政策方針的最終措辭預定於7月稍晚公布，則是另一項獨立考驗，用以觀察政府打算為日本央行保留多少政策空間。

馬來西亞國家銀行將於7月9日當地時間15:00公布利率決策。25位受訪經濟學家中有24位預期隔夜政策利率維持在2.75%，僅1位預期升息25個基點。第一季經濟成長5.4%、人工智慧相關出口強勁，以及馬來西亞令吉6月貶值近3%，都為央行發出更偏鷹訊號提供空間；但燃料補貼已壓抑國內通膨，央行也依靠鼓勵外匯流入的措施。政策取捨將決定馬來西亞是加入區域緊縮行列，還是繼續認為無須立即升息便能管控輸入型壓力。

波蘭央行總裁Adam Glapinski於7月9日舉行的簡報，將說明通膨預測上修是否排除了2026年剩餘時間降息的可能。7月10日公布的德國CPI終值，將檢視初值年增2.3%、月減0.3%的組成，包括核心通膨是否仍接近2.5%。加拿大同日公布的6月勞動力調查，則將更新加拿大央行關注的就業、工資及勞動參與資訊。

美國最重要的事件仍是7月14日公布的6月CPI及實質薪資。整體與核心通膨將顯示，在最新一波油價反彈前，先前能源價格下跌是否帶來足夠緩解；實質薪資則衡量家庭購買力所受壓力。聯準會會議紀要已表明，能源、關稅或強勁需求造成的持續性通膨可能構成再次升息的理由；CPI將是檢驗這項情境機率上升或下降的第一項重要數據。

油價與荷莫茲海峽情勢仍是串連上述事件的共同條件。7月15日公布的下一份EIA石油報告，將顯示煉油廠產能利用率維持目前高檔之際，汽油及餾分油庫存是否繼續收緊。若原油持續上漲、成品油庫存又進一步下降，地緣政治干擾傳導至消費者物價的作用將增強；若航運恢復、成品油庫存回升，央行則可把波動性的地緣政治溢價與持久通膨區分開來。

overall_summary.headline: 伊朗衝突再起、聯準會鷹派情境使升息時點提前，美債延續賣壓
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國再度發動空襲、與伊朗的臨時停火破裂，加上石油銷售豁免遭撤銷，推動布蘭特原油上漲5.21%至$78.02，WTI上漲4.37%至$73.52，美債也延續賣壓。2年期殖利率上升3.3個基點至4.22%，5年期上升3.9個基點至4.328%，10年期上升2.9個基點至4.581%，30年期上升1.7個基點至5.074%。短、中天期承受較大壓力，市場將聯準會下一次預期升息時點由12月提前至10月。

聯準會6月會議紀要顯示，少數官員當時已認為有理由升息，但決策委員會仍一致將利率維持於3.5%至3.75%。9位與會者預期2026年至少升息一次，其中6位預期至少升息兩次；另外9位則預期利率不變或調降。油價使這項分歧前景更為急迫：即使美國原油庫存增加300萬桶，餾分油庫存仍減少500萬桶，降至比5年同期平均低約12%；約6,300萬桶伊朗原油則滯留海上或等待買家。

本次走勢主要是實質利率重定價，而非通膨預期全面上升。10年期實質殖利率上升2.4個基點至2.305%，10年期損益兩平通膨率僅上升0.5個基點至2.276%。不過，增額發行的$390億10年期公債需求仍然穩健，得標殖利率較標售前交易低約0.6個基點，投標倍數為2.59倍。股市走勢分歧、黃金下跌，信用市場也僅小幅轉弱，顯示風險趨避具選擇性，並非系統性撤退。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries extended their selloff on July 8 as the breakdown of the U.S.-Iran ceasefire drove oil sharply higher and the Federal Reserve’s June minutes showed that policy tightening had become an active, if divided, Committee scenario. The 2-year yield rose 3.3 basis points to 4.22%, the 5-year climbed 3.9 basis points to 4.328%, the 10-year increased 2.9 basis points to 4.581%, and the 30-year added 1.7 basis points to 5.074%. The pressure was again broad, but the concentration in shorter and intermediate maturities reflected a market bringing the next possible Fed increase forward rather than treating the geopolitical escalation solely as a long-run inflation or fiscal shock.

President Donald Trump declared the interim ceasefire with Iran effectively over after the U.S. launched fresh strikes and revoked a waiver that had allowed Iranian oil sales. Brent crude rose 5.21% to $78.02 and WTI gained 4.37% to $73.52. The waiver reversal also left roughly 63 million barrels of Iranian crude at sea or awaiting buyers, while renewed threats to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz raised the risk that readily available supply would tighten even if aggregate global production remained ample.

The domestic inventory picture added a material qualification to the headline increase in U.S. crude stocks. Commercial crude inventories rose 3 million barrels in the week ended July 3, but gasoline fell 1.9 million and distillates dropped 5 million as refinery utilization reached 95.8%. Distillate stocks stood about 12% below their 5-year seasonal average. That product scarcity made a renewed oil shock more relevant for delivered fuel costs than the crude build alone suggested.

Fed minutes reinforced the rates move. A few officials had seen a case for increasing the federal funds rate at the June 16–17 meeting, although the Committee unanimously held it at 3.5%–3.75%. Policymakers generally judged that upside inflation risks remained elevated while downside employment risks had moderated somewhat. Their projections were evenly divided at the broadest level: 9 officials expected at least one quarter-point increase during 2026, including 6 who anticipated at least two, while another 9 expected either no change or a reduction. Chair Kevin Warsh submitted no forecast.

The market response was not an indiscriminate inflation trade. The 10-year real yield rose 2.4 basis points to 2.305%, while the 10-year breakeven increased only 0.5 basis point to 2.276%. Most of the rise in the nominal benchmark therefore came through the real-rate component, consistent with greater confidence that the Fed would respond to persistent inflation rather than tolerate a sustained increase in expectations. The 2s10s curve narrowed 0.4 basis point to 36.1 basis points and 2s30s flattened 1.6 basis points to 85.4 basis points.

Demand at the Treasury’s $39 billion 10-year reopening nevertheless remained firm. The note was awarded at 4.580%, about 0.6 basis point below its yield in pre-auction trading, with a 2.59 bid-to-cover ratio. Indirect bidders received $31.721 billion of accepted competitive tenders, while primary dealers took $3.027 billion. Investors were willing to add duration at the higher yield even as oil, hawkish policy scenarios and exceptional corporate issuance kept the broader discount-rate backdrop under pressure.

Risk assets did not produce a broad flight into government bonds. The S&P 500 recovered most of an early decline and closed 0.28% lower, while the Nasdaq 100 gained 0.27% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 2.23%. Gold fell 1.79% despite the geopolitical escalation, and the dollar index slipped 0.09%. Listed investment-grade, high-yield and emerging-market debt funds declined by roughly 0.13% to 0.19%, while credit-default swap spreads widened from unusually tight levels. The session combined renewed inflation risk and higher real yields with selective rather than systemic risk aversion.

## Oil and the Fed Pull the Policy Horizon Forward

The immediate repricing began with a deterioration in the political and physical conditions surrounding the Strait of Hormuz. Trump said negotiations with Iran had become a waste of time and threatened additional strikes and a renewed blockade of Iranian ports. The U.S. had already attacked more than 80 sites and revoked the temporary waiver under which Iran had been allowed to sell oil. Tehran, which had accused Washington of violating the interim agreement, warned of retaliation and maintained that vessels could not pass through the strait without its permission.

Brent traded above $79 during the U.S. session and briefly exceeded $80 in subsequent trading. The rise reversed part of the relief that followed the June truce, although Brent remained 16.19% lower over one month and WTI was down 18.80%. The policy issue was therefore not a return to the wartime price peak, but another interruption to the rapid disinflationary reversal that had encouraged investors to push the next expected Fed increase later in the year.

The revocation of the oil-sales waiver complicated the supply picture beyond the immediate risk to tanker traffic. About 63 million barrels of Iranian crude were already on vessels in the Persian Gulf and across Asian waters, with many ships showing no clear destination or advertising availability. At least 19 Iranian oil and petrochemical cargoes had loaded after the interim deal, while another 46 laden tankers were identified near Iran’s coastline.

Prospective buyers had already been cautious because European and British restrictions remained in place, insurance was difficult, and ports could refuse vessels associated with Iran’s dark fleet. Refiners in Japan, Taiwan and South Korea had received offers without recording purchases, while Indian processors had been prepared to buy only if the U.S. waiver extended beyond August. Chinese independent refiners remained a possible outlet, but competing Saudi and Iraqi supply meant Tehran would probably have to offer substantial discounts. The waiver’s withdrawal therefore removed revenue Iran had been promised under the peace arrangement while leaving a large volume of oil commercially stranded.

U.S. petroleum data showed why the market focused on product availability as well as crude supply. Commercial crude inventories excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve rose to 411.4 million barrels but remained about 6% below their 5-year seasonal average. Gasoline inventories also stood roughly 6% below average after their weekly decline. Distillate stocks fell to 103.6 million barrels, about 12% below the seasonal norm, and total commercial petroleum inventories decreased by 4 million barrels. Refineries processed an average 17 million barrels a day at 95.8% utilization, limiting the near-term capacity to compensate for further product losses simply by raising run rates.

That combination sharpened the inflation channel. A geopolitical premium in crude can fade quickly if threatened supply continues to reach buyers, but depleted gasoline and distillate inventories make a disruption more likely to reach retail and transportation costs. Average U.S. gasoline prices had already climbed above $4.56 a gallon in May before retreating almost 17% to $3.79 by July 6. The latest oil rebound threatened part of that improvement without yet establishing another sustained surge.

The June Fed minutes supplied the reaction function against which the energy risk was priced. Officials said that inflation remained elevated and generally assessed risks to price stability as skewed upward. At the same time, several labor indicators suggested employment was stable, and concern about a material weakening in maximum employment had moderated. The Committee continued to expect solid real GDP growth through the rest of 2026.

Policymakers considered distinctly different paths rather than converging on an unconditional increase. Under a scenario in which inflation moderated, most expected to maintain or eventually lower the target range. Under another scenario involving persistent inflation from strong artificial-intelligence-related demand, high energy prices and tariffs, most thought some further firming would probably be needed. The minutes therefore supported higher yields by confirming that another increase was a live response to persistent pressure, while preserving the possibility of a hold or eventual reduction if inflation subsided.

The distribution of individual projections underscored the lack of consensus. Nine participants foresaw at least one increase this year, with 6 expecting at least two. The remaining 9 expected no increase or a cut, and Warsh declined to contribute a projection. A few officials thought the case for raising rates was already present in June, yet they joined the unanimous vote to hold. That distinction matters: the minutes revealed a more hawkish risk distribution, not a decision already made for the next meeting.

Markets responded by bringing the expected timing of the next increase forward to October from December. One intraday measure put the probability of an increase at the July meeting near 33%, while another placed it above 30%, up from less than 20% the previous Thursday. Broader pricing implied more than one quarter-point increase by year-end. Those probabilities were recorded before the path of the renewed conflict and energy prices could be known, leaving the geopolitical outcome unusually important to the policy timetable.

The real-yield move was consistent with that interpretation. The 10-year TIPS yield reached 2.305%, its highest area since April 2025 and 14.3 basis points above its level a month earlier. Ten-year inflation compensation rose only modestly on July 8 and remained 9.3 basis points below its month-earlier level. Investors demanded a higher inflation-adjusted return as they priced a firmer central-bank response, while the decline in crude from its earlier wartime highs continued to restrain longer-horizon inflation compensation.

The shift occurred in active trading. FINRA recorded $1.441 trillion of Treasury par activity, 20.7% more than the previous session, with nominal-coupon activity rising 24.4% to $1.1402 trillion. Activity in maturities longer than 7 years and no more than 10 years increased 41.8% to $225.9 billion, while TIPS activity rose 55.6% to $23.5 billion. Those figures measure two-way turnover, but they show that the repricing and auction concession developed in a heavily traded market.

## Firm Wholesale Sales, Weak Card Credit and Strong Auction Demand

U.S. activity evidence did not offer a simple offset to the inflation risk. May wholesale sales rose 3.4% from April to $817.4 billion and were 18.1% higher than a year earlier. April’s monthly increase was revised to 2.2% from 2%. Inventories rose only 0.1% to $941.8 billion, leaving them 4% above the previous year, and the inventories-to-sales ratio fell to 1.15 from 1.31 in May 2025.

The combination points to strong nominal turnover and a leaner stock of goods relative to sales. It strengthens the current-quarter growth input from wholesale activity, while the low inventory ratio leaves businesses with less cushion if supply disruption or higher transportation costs interrupt replenishment. The report did not establish how much of the sales increase reflected volumes rather than prices, but it was not evidence of a broad collapse in demand.

Consumer credit provided a contrasting household signal. Total credit was unchanged at a seasonally adjusted annual rate in May after a revised 4.9% increase in April. The annualized flow was negative $2.2 billion after a revised positive $249.9 billion, leaving seasonally adjusted credit outstanding at $5.1545 trillion.

The composition was weaker than the total alone. Revolving credit, which includes credit-card balances, contracted at a 4.7% annual rate, while nonrevolving credit grew 1.6%. The reversal in card borrowing suggests that household spending was receiving less support from short-term credit even as wholesale sales remained strong. It also marked a different transmission channel from oil: higher fuel costs can squeeze discretionary cash flow precisely when consumers are no longer expanding revolving balances.

Treasury supply showed no comparable loss of demand. The $39 billion reopening of the 10-year note was awarded at 4.580%, the highest auction yield for the tenor since February 2025, and stopped about 0.6 basis point through pre-sale trading. The 2.59 bid-to-cover ratio was accompanied by $31.721 billion of indirect awards, $4.175 billion to direct bidders and $3.027 billion to primary dealers. The note settles July 15 and matures May 15, 2036.

The result did not reverse the day’s selloff, but it demonstrated that buyers were willing to absorb benchmark duration once the yield approached 4.6%. Indirect accounts dominated the accepted competitive awards, while the limited dealer allocation reduced the immediate inventory left with intermediaries. That demand was notable because the auction arrived after a large rise in yields over the preceding week and amid a global selloff rather than a flight-to-quality rally.

The 17-week bill auction also attracted substantial cash demand. Treasury sold $72 billion of 119-day bills at a 3.790% high rate and 3.891% investment rate. The bid-to-cover ratio was 3.41, with $243.646 billion of competitive tenders submitted and $70.371 billion accepted. Indirect bidders received $48.986 billion, direct bidders $3.158 billion and primary dealers $18.227 billion. The issue settles July 14 and matures November 10.

The bill result did not show visible funding stress at the 4-month point, although it belongs to a different part of the curve from the Fed-sensitive 2-year note. Cash investors were willing to bid more than three times the offered amount even as the market assigned greater probability to another policy increase. The large share allotted at the 3.790% high rate—80.43%—described the auction’s concentration at that stop rather than weakness relative to a pre-auction reference.

The next supply test moves much farther out the curve. Treasury will reopen $22 billion of the 5% bond on July 9, with 29 years and 10 months remaining to maturity. The sale settles July 15 alongside the 10-year reopening. With the 30-year yield already above 5%, the auction will test whether the demand visible in the benchmark note extends to duration carrying greater fiscal and term-premium exposure.

## Global Tightening Signals Spread Across Developed and Emerging Markets

The U.S. move formed part of a wider global bond selloff. European yields rose more sharply as investors increased wagers on further tightening by the European Central Bank and Bank of England. The 10-year gilt yield jumped 10 basis points to 4.95%, its highest in nearly a month. The synchronized move made the Treasury selloff more than a local response to U.S. data, even though oil and Fed minutes supplied its strongest domestic catalysts.

New Zealand delivered a realized tightening decision. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand increased its Official Cash Rate by 25 basis points to 2.5%, its first increase in 3 years, and indicated that further reductions in monetary stimulus could be required because inflation remained above target and activity was expected to strengthen. The New Zealand dollar and government-bond yields rose after the announcement. The decision reinforced the global repricing toward tighter policy, while reflecting the RBNZ’s domestic assessment rather than a common timetable across central banks.

Poland held its policy rate at 3.75% for a fourth consecutive month, matching all 29 economist forecasts, but raised its inflation projections. The central bank now expects consumer-price growth of 2.4%–3.3% in 2026, compared with a March range of 1.6%–2.9%, while its growth range was adjusted to 3%–4.4% from 3.1%–4.7%. Inflation had slowed to 2.5% in June, but Middle East uncertainty and energy costs made an early return to easing less likely.

Forward-rate agreements rose 4 basis points and indicated that Poland’s policy rate could remain unchanged for the rest of 2026. The revised forecast reduced the significance of headline inflation returning to the central bank’s target area: policymakers no longer faced a clear case for further tightening, but the projected path was not benign enough to resume cuts. Governor Adam Glapinski’s July 9 briefing will show whether officials emphasize the improvement in current inflation or the renewed external price risk.

Romania also held rates, leaving its benchmark at 6.5%, the highest in the European Union, in line with unanimous expectations. Inflation had moved back above 10% in May as the earlier energy shock compounded the effects of taxes and the removal of an electricity-price cap. The central bank expects inflation to decline slightly in June and then fall substantially in the third quarter as those base effects fade, with fiscal consolidation weighing on demand over a longer horizon.

That prospective disinflation is vulnerable to politics and fiscal execution. Romania is governed by a caretaker administration after Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan lost a confidence vote, and parties have failed to agree on a successor cabinet. Prolonged legislative paralysis could impede measures needed to secure EU recovery funds and heighten downgrade risk for a sovereign already at the lowest investment-grade level with negative outlooks from all 3 major rating companies.

Chile delivered a more immediate inflation surprise. Consumer prices were unchanged in June from May, compared with expectations for a 0.2% decline, and annual inflation accelerated to 4.3%, its highest since September and above the 3% target. Energy prices fell 1.1% and transportation declined 1.3%, helped by cheaper fuel, while clothing dropped 6.1% during Cyber Day promotions. Food and non-alcoholic beverages rose 0.8%, offsetting that relief.

The release showed that weak activity was not yet producing broad disinflation. Chile’s economic-activity index had declined in May after barely growing in April, unemployment had reached 9.4%, and analysts expected GDP growth of only 1.6% in 2026. Yet 2-year swaps rose 10 basis points to 4.46% after the CPI report, and the combination of food pressure and renewed global energy risk supported the central bank’s cautious decision to keep its policy rate at 4.5%.

Japan’s bond market faced an unusually direct clash between strong credit activity, political influence over monetary policy and unresolved fiscal financing. Bank lending rose 6.3% from a year earlier in June, the fastest pace since August 2020, driven by mergers and acquisitions, real estate and economic recovery. The result indicated that credit remained accessible despite the BOJ’s June increase in its benchmark rate to 1%.

The lending data strengthened the case that the economy could withstand further normalization. Business assessments of financial conditions had improved for the first time in a year, and large companies reported better conditions for commercial-paper issuance. Japan’s real policy rate remained below zero, while a BOJ estimate put underlying inflation above 2% after excluding transitory factors and fresh food. Private forecasts nevertheless differed on the eventual destination: economists surveyed after the June meeting expected a 1.75% terminal rate, while BNP Paribas projected 2.5% and increases roughly every 4 to 5 months.

Government language did little to relieve pressure on longer JGBs. An updated draft of the annual economic and fiscal agenda added a call for monetary policy that contributes to stable price increases, a phrase that can be read as allowing the BOJ to raise rates when needed. The earlier draft had emphasized the importance of appropriate monetary conduct without referring to inflation, prompting concern that Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s administration wanted to restrain further increases.

The revision did not halt the selloff. Yields on 10- and 20-year JGBs reached their highest levels since 1996 as investors continued to focus on Takaichi’s ¥370 trillion public-and-private investment goal for 17 strategic industries through fiscal 2040 and the lack of clarity about the government’s share of its financing. BOJ board member Toichiro Asada, a Takaichi appointee and the sole dissenter against June’s rate increase, separately warned that higher rates could slow the economy. Ayano Sato, another appointee viewed as a reflationist, will attend her first meeting at the end of July.

Moody’s said Japan’s A1 rating and stable outlook remained balanced for now. It cited steady growth, sustained inflation and a projected decline in government debt below 195% of GDP by 2030 from about 219% in fiscal 2020. The agency nevertheless identified recurring spending, weaker fiscal consolidation and insufficient private participation in the investment program as potential risks. Its assessment did not remove the market’s concern that simultaneous fiscal expansion and restraints on BOJ normalization could entrench inflation and yen weakness.

China’s sovereign market presented the opposite demand problem. The bid-to-cover ratio at a 10-year government-bond auction reached a record 7.23 in data going back to 2004. The average yield was 1.7249%, the high yield 1.7418%, and comparable bonds traded near 1.728% in the secondary market. Banks continued to seek bond allocations amid weak loan demand, while the removal of primary-market fee rebates made auction pricing more transparent and created an arbitrage opportunity where auction yields exceeded secondary levels.

## Credit Investors Absorb Supply but Demand More Discrimination

Credit markets weakened modestly as the ceasefire failed, but the price action remained far from a generalized funding seizure. Investment-grade LQD fell 0.19%, high-yield HYG declined 0.13%, JNK lost 0.16%, and emerging-market debt fund EMB dropped 0.16%. Credit-default swap spreads widened from levels close to post-financial-crisis lows in both the U.S. and Europe. The move showed that geopolitical risk could disturb historically rich valuations even when cash-bond losses remained limited.

Investor behavior has already begun to adjust to that narrow margin for error. Assets in U.S. nontraditional bond funds have grown about 6% this year and 18% since the end of 2024, while European global flexible-bond funds have expanded almost 10% in 2026. These strategies can move across government debt, corporate bonds, subordinated instruments and derivatives instead of buying securities according to their weight in an index. Their revival reflects both attractive all-in yields and greater discomfort with uniformly tight credit spreads.

Heavy technology issuance is intensifying the distinction between issuer quality and market capacity. Amazon’s $25 billion transaction attracted $41 billion of orders, or 1.6 times the deal’s size, compared with 4.7 times for an earlier Amazon sale in February. The company has issued more than $90 billion of bonds this year, contributing to about $194 billion of new hyperscaler debt.

Bank of America analysts estimated that the Amazon sale pushed spreads on existing hyperscaler bonds 6–15 basis points wider during the previous session and added about 8 basis points to that day’s increase in the 10-year Treasury yield. The estimate reframes large artificial-intelligence financing as a rates-market issue as well as a sector credit story: dealers and investors must fund and hedge duration at a scale capable of affecting the government benchmark against which the bonds are priced.

That does not mean buyers have withdrawn. Amazon completed the financing, semiconductor shares rebounded on July 8, and all-in corporate yields remain well above their longer-run averages. It does mean repeated megadeals are requiring more balance-sheet capacity and price sensitivity. Passive credit investors are particularly exposed because an issuer’s index weight rises as it borrows more, potentially concentrating portfolios in the companies creating the most new supply.

Stress at weaker issuers was much more explicit. Aston Martin’s $1.05 billion of secured notes due in 2029 fell about 4 cents to roughly 72 cents on the dollar as more than half of its secured noteholders formed a cooperation group. The group, advised by Akin Gump, remains open to other secured creditors. Its formation gives bondholders a common negotiating structure while earnings pressure forces the luxury-car maker to cut jobs, review new models and seek unconventional sources of cash.

Victoria reached a restructuring agreement with holders of notes due in 2028 who had been excluded from an earlier transaction. Consenting holders will receive 75% of the face value of their securities in new second-priority bonds due in 2031 and about 19% of the company’s equity. A group holding two-thirds of the £166.6 million of outstanding notes supports the plan. Investors who join within 10 business days can receive an early-consent fee; those who do not consent face having their bonds written down to zero.

The carpet maker also agreed terms with Koch, which will exchange £380 million of preferred instruments for £50 million of preferred shares, a 25% ordinary-equity stake and new second-priority bonds due in 2031. Victoria expects the combined restructuring to reduce debt and preferred liabilities by more than £300 million. The transaction resolves part of the creditor dispute created by last year’s uptiering, but it does so through substantial concessions and equity dilution rather than a return to ordinary refinancing.

Sovereign borrowers displayed a wider range of funding choices. Argentina secured the money for a $4.3 billion semiannual foreign-currency bond payment due July 9 and identified financing sources intended to cover obligations through the end of President Javier Milei’s term in 2027 without relying on international issuance. Treasury dollar deposits of about $4 billion and incoming multilateral-backed financing will fund the immediate payment.

Argentina has raised roughly $4 billion since March through locally issued dollar bonds maturing in 2027 and 2028 at an average yield of 6.9%, below the roughly 8.6% investors estimate it would pay internationally. The lower domestic cost explains the government’s reluctance to demonstrate global market access merely for its own sake. The risk is that the 2027 plan leaves little room for failure: about $25 billion comes due next year, to be met with local bond sales, central-bank dollar purchases, IMF disbursements, privatization proceeds and cash carried over from 2026.

Bangladesh is at an earlier stage of market development. The government will form an inter-ministerial panel to study the structure, timing and feasibility of its first overseas sovereign bond. Officials have not chosen a size or currency, though a conventional dollar issue is the principal option and a panda bond was also discussed. The proposed borrowing would diversify funding beyond domestic banks and concessional multilateral loans as the government plans a 19% increase in spending, but it would also expose its fiscal program to direct international pricing and ratings scrutiny.

Johannesburg, meanwhile, plans to pay nearly 2.4 billion rand owed to creditors including Rand Water and Eskom by mid-July in order to restore withheld government transfers. South Africa’s Treasury withheld 13.5 billion rand from 69 municipalities and will initially release only about one-third of the money after acceptable repayment plans are submitted. Remaining funds depend partly on reducing unauthorized, irregular and wasteful expenditure by at least 25% by the end of September. Mayor Dada Morero said the city is also preparing a bond sale to finance infrastructure repairs, but transaction advisers and final terms have yet to be arranged.

## Forward Market Significance

The first U.S. test on July 9 is initial unemployment insurance claims at 08:30 ET. The release will show whether the labor market remains characterized by slower hiring and reduced mobility without a broader increase in layoffs. That distinction is central to the Fed minutes: officials had become slightly less concerned about downside employment risk, giving persistent inflation more weight in their reaction function.

June existing-home sales follow at 10:00 ET. Sales and inventory will provide a current measure of housing’s sensitivity to mortgage rates as Treasury yields move higher again. The result will also help distinguish the contraction in May revolving credit from a broader household-demand slowdown.

Treasury’s $22 billion reopening of the 5% 30-year bond at 13:00 ET is the immediate duration event. The security has 29 years and 10 months remaining and settles July 15. The 10-year reopening attracted strong indirect demand and cleared below its pre-auction yield, but the long bond carries greater exposure to fiscal uncertainty, term premium and the durability of inflation. Its stop relative to pre-sale trading and the distribution among indirect, direct and dealer bidders will determine whether Wednesday’s demand extends to the end of the curve.

The BOJ’s July regional economic report will update evidence on wages, prices and activity across Japan after bank lending grew 6.3% and longer JGB yields reached multi-decade highs. The report bears directly on whether accommodative financial conditions still justify further normalization despite political concern about higher borrowing costs. The final wording of the government’s annual policy agenda, due later in July, remains a separate test of how much room the administration intends to leave the BOJ.

Bank Negara Malaysia announces its decision at 15:00 local time on July 9. Twenty-four of 25 surveyed economists expect the overnight policy rate to remain at 2.75%, while one expects a 25-basis-point increase. First-quarter growth of 5.4%, strong artificial-intelligence-related exports and a nearly 3% June decline in the ringgit create scope for a more hawkish signal, but fuel subsidies have contained domestic inflation and the central bank has relied on measures to encourage foreign-exchange inflows. The balance will determine whether Malaysia joins the regional tightening moves or continues to treat imported pressure as manageable without an immediate rate increase.

Polish Governor Adam Glapinski’s briefing on July 9 will clarify whether the raised inflation forecast closes the door to easing for the rest of 2026. German final CPI on July 10 will test the composition of the provisional 2.3% annual and negative 0.3% monthly readings, including whether core inflation remains near 2.5%. Canada’s June labor-force survey the same day will update employment, wages and participation for the Bank of Canada.

The dominant U.S. event remains June CPI and real earnings on July 14. Headline and core inflation will show whether the earlier decline in energy prices delivered enough relief before the latest rebound, while real earnings will measure the pressure on household purchasing power. The minutes established that persistent inflation from energy, tariffs or strong demand could warrant another Fed increase; CPI will provide the first major test of whether that scenario is becoming more or less likely.

Oil and Hormuz remain the condition linking those events. The next EIA petroleum report on July 15 will show whether gasoline and distillate inventories continue to tighten while refineries operate near current utilization rates. A sustained rise in crude accompanied by further product draws would strengthen the transmission from geopolitical disruption to consumer prices. Restored shipping and rebuilt product stocks would instead allow central banks to separate a volatile geopolitical premium from durable inflation.

Low product inventories strengthened the fuel-inflation channel, while firm 10-year auction demand and mixed risk assets showed that the session was not a generalized flight from duration or credit.

Consumer credit was unchanged at an annual rate and revolving balances contracted 4.7%, suggesting less support for spending from cards. Treasury demand remained strong: the $39 billion 10-year reopening stopped through pre-sale trading, and the 17-week bill sale drew bids exceeding three times the amount offered.

section_summaries.section_title: Global Tightening Signals Spread Across Developed and Emerging Markets
section_summaries.summary: The global selloff broadened as European yields rose and New Zealand lifted its policy rate 25 basis points to 2.5%. Poland and Romania held rates but faced renewed inflation risks, while Chilean inflation accelerated to 4.3%. Strong Japanese lending and unresolved fiscal financing pushed long JGB yields to their highest since 1996; China instead recorded a 7.23 bid-to-cover ratio at its 10-year auction as banks sought bonds amid weak loan demand.

section_summaries.market_read: Megadeals can lift Treasury yields as investors fund and hedge duration, making corporate supply a rates catalyst.
section_summaries.section_title: Credit Investors Absorb Supply but Demand More Discrimination
section_summaries.summary: Credit weakened modestly from rich valuations as default-swap spreads widened and investors absorbed heavy issuance with greater price sensitivity. Amazon’s $25 billion sale drew $41 billion of orders, only 1.6 times the deal versus 4.7 times in February, and pressured existing hyperscaler spreads. Aston Martin’s creditor group and Victoria’s concessionary restructuring showed sharper stress among weaker issuers, while Argentina relied on domestic funding for its July 9 payment.

July 9 brings U.S. jobless claims, home sales and the 30-year reopening, alongside BOJ regional evidence, Malaysia’s rate decision and Poland’s guidance. German CPI and Canadian labor data follow July 10. The dominant U.S. test is June CPI and real earnings on July 14, followed by the July 15 petroleum report; inflation, long-duration demand and oil-product availability will determine whether the earlier Fed timetable and higher real yields endure.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries extend their selloff as renewed Iran conflict and hawkish Fed scenarios pull rate-increase timing forward
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries extended their selloff as renewed U.S. strikes, the collapse of the interim Iran ceasefire and the withdrawal of an oil-sales waiver pushed Brent up 5.21% to $78.02 and WTI up 4.37% to $73.52. The 2-year yield rose 3.3 basis points to 4.22%, the 5-year climbed 3.9 basis points to 4.328%, the 10-year increased 2.9 basis points to 4.581%, and the 30-year added 1.7 basis points to 5.074%. Shorter and intermediate maturities led the pressure as markets brought the expected timing of the next Fed increase forward to October from December.

June Fed minutes showed that a few officials had already seen a case for raising rates, although the Committee unanimously held at 3.5%–3.75%. Nine participants expected at least one increase during 2026, including 6 who expected at least two, while another 9 anticipated no change or a reduction. Oil added urgency to that divided outlook: about 63 million barrels of Iranian crude were stranded or awaiting buyers, and U.S. distillate stocks fell 5 million barrels to about 12% below their 5-year seasonal average despite a 3 million-barrel crude build.

The move was primarily a real-rate repricing rather than a broad inflation-expectations shock. The 10-year real yield rose 2.4 basis points to 2.305%, while the 10-year breakeven increased only 0.5 basis point to 2.276%. Demand nevertheless remained firm at the $39 billion 10-year reopening, which stopped about 0.6 basis point through pre-auction trading with a 2.59 bid-to-cover ratio. Mixed equities, falling gold and only modest credit weakness indicated selective rather than systemic risk aversion.
overall_summary.summary: Treasury yields rose across the curve as renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities lifted oil and June Fed minutes put further tightening in play, with the move concentrated in real yields even as the 10-year auction drew firm demand.
